reported_design_fact: ChatGPT was part of the scored creative problem-solving task; a separate AI-removal assessment was not reported.
published_result_relevance: Illustrates assistance-contingent joint performance rather than an assistance-independent post-assistance outcome.

reported_design_fact: A randomized experiment examined what happened when AI feedback assistance was removed and whether self-regulation supports could substitute for it.
published_result_relevance: Illustrates the distinction between assistance availability, learner agency, and performance after assistance changes.

reported_design_fact: Students were randomized to use ChatGPT or Google during information gathering; the study compared mental effort and depth of scientific reasoning.
published_result_relevance: Illustrates why cognitive-effort and reasoning-process measures complement outcome-level assistance metadata.

reported_design_fact: ChatGPT-supported learning was followed by separately reported knowledge-gain and transfer outcomes.
published_result_relevance: Illustrates why supported task performance and later learning outcomes should be reported separately.

reported_design_fact: Participants completed a three-item post-test after the hint phase; the post-test repeated the pre-test items.
published_result_relevance: Illustrates why item novelty and transfer distance must be reported separately.

reported_design_fact: AI-assisted practice was followed by a closed-book, closed-laptop exam on conceptually similar problems.
published_result_relevance: Provides separate supported and assistance-removed randomized outcomes under standard and guarded GPT architectures.

reported_design_fact: AI-supported lessons were followed by objective post-tests completed without the tutor during the test.
published_result_relevance: Illustrates immediate assistance-removed assessment under a pedagogically designed AI tutor.

reported_design_fact: AI-supported programming exercises were followed by knowledge and code-comprehension assessment.
published_result_relevance: Illustrates dissociation between supported exercise performance and later knowledge/comprehension outcomes.

reported_design_fact: AI-assisted creative work was followed by a subsequent independent creative task; one condition required thinking before ChatGPT use.
A surprise assessment was administered 45 days after the study phase.
published_result_relevance: Illustrates why exact elapsed time should be reported before making a retention interpretation.

reported_design_fact: The knowledge questionnaire was administered again at six-week follow-up; participants were instructed to complete the digital follow-up independently.
published_result_relevance: Illustrates an assistance-removal condition with instruction-based rather than strongly verified independence.

reported_design_fact: Theoretical knowledge was assessed at six-month follow-up; the accessible report does not explicitly establish AI non-availability during that assessment.
published_result_relevance: Illustrates why exact timing does not substitute for explicit assistance-status and independence-evidence reporting.
